newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INSTANT VIEW-RBA September quarter Bulletin.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INSTANT VIEW-RBA September quarter Bulletin.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia released its September quarter Bulletin at 3.00 p.m. (0500 GMT), a report that has given more emphasis than usual as the financial markets have widely been expecting a further reduction in official interest rates in the next few weeks.
The RBA said that low inflation expectations would support a case for lower interest rates, but that an easing would depend on wages growth.
The bank said some wage agreements were based on higher than actual inflation. It also said a case for lower rates would be strengthened if the economy was weaker than expected.
The following are a selection of econimists' immediate reactions to the RBA Bulletin.
STEPHEN ROBERTS, CHIEF ECONOMIST, UBS AUSTRLIA:

"I'm still tipping an interest rate cut on November 6, but not with as greater confidence as before. Quite clearly the Reserve Bank has some concerns about wages. But providing the average weekly earnings and CPI report are sufficiently low I don't think they will stand in the way of this rate cut. I don't think people should be looking for any more beyond that."
